referenceMaterial.summary: Add columns as NULLABLE first without defaults, backfill existing records in small asynchronous batches, and set the default constraint subsequently. In modern PostgreSQL (11+), ensure defaults are non-volatile constants. Invariant: "Production schema migrations must use backward-compatible, zero- rewrite DDL steps (nullable columns, phased backfills)."
approachSteps: 1. Ingress Boundary Defense: Add columns as NULLABLE first without defaults, backfill existing records in small asynchronous batches, and set the default constraint subsequently.
2. Failure Containment: Eliminate unconstrained buffering and propagate physical backpressure.
3. Invariant Enforcement: Production schema migrations must use backward-compatible, zero- rewrite DDL steps (nullable columns, phased backfills).

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: In older relational engines (or PostgreSQL versions without default metadata rewrites), adding a column with a volatile default forces a full table rewrite, acquiring an exclusive table lock for 20 minutes and rejecting all traffic.
Breakdown Chain: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Production schema migrations must use backward-compatible, zero- rewrite DDL steps (nullable columns, phased backfills)."

approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
